FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
PRESS ADVISORY
See: IS THE DRUG WAR FOREVER? VCL forum to be held in Boston on Thursday, January 29.

Please Contact: Michael D. Cutler, Esq.
Phone: (617) 739-9093

Experts Take Critical Look at the Effectiveness of the Drug War: "Is the Drug War Forever?"

On Thursday, January 29, 1998 beginning at 6PM, at the C. Walsh Theater, Suffolk University, on Temple Street (behind the Massachusetts State House) a public forum will be held evaluating the effectiveness of the nation's current drug policies. The forum will feature Anthony Lewis, Pulitzer Prize winning

New York Times columnist; the Hon. Nancy Gertner, United States District Court Judge for the District of Mass.; David C. Lewis, M.D., Director of the Center for Alcohol and Addiction Studies at Brown University and Project Director for the Physicians' Leadership on National Drug policy. The forum is being produced by the Voluntary Committee of Lawyers.

With the declaration of the war against drugs 25 years ago, the United States embarked upon a pursuit noble in motive and far-reaching in consequence. As with alcohol prohibition, however, attempts at enforcement have clogged the courts, filled the prisons, corrupted officials at home and abroad, bred disrespect for the law in important communities, imperiled the liberties of the people, squandered precious public resources and brought the nation no closer to abstinence. This forum is convened to examine the drug war's effectiveness and the need to develop alternate strategies for reducing the harm caused by drugs, without the adverse side effects of the current policy.

The forum is produced by the Voluntary Committee of Lawyers (VCL). The original VCL was formed by corporate lawyers in 1927, who found the courts, law enforcement, the national economy and public safety dangerously impaired by alcohol prohibition. They organized first in NYC, then nationally (over 3000 members by 1933). This group drafted the repeal plank in FDR's platform at the 1932 Democratic Convention, then helped to engineer passage of the Prohibition Repeal Amendment in only 8 months.

The new VCL (of which Elliot Richardson is a co-founder; he was presented with the Medal of Freedom by Pres. Clinton January 15, 1998) seeks not to legalize any particular drug, but rather to legalize public discourse regarding the failure of our current drug abuse control policies, without dissenters being demonized as encouraging drug use. The current system is unaffordably expensive, racially punitive and no obstacle to adolescent drug access. VCL members believe we as a people, by encouraging open discussion of drug war alternatives, can and must develop a better national policy.

Federal drug policy, that officially ignores the success of the public health models in Holland and Switzerland, discourages the reasonable assessment of alternate policies. These views are largely shared by Mass. former SJC (state supreme appellate court) chief justices Paul Liacos and Ed Hennessey, Pres. Reagan's Secretary of State George Schultz, Pres. Johnson's AG (and former IBM chief counsel) Nick Katzenbach, first federal circuit (Boston) chief judge Juan Torreulla, and Chicago federal circuit chief judge Richard Posner.

On January 5, 1998, panel moderator Anthony Lewis wrote an OpEd piece for the New York Times entitled, The Noble Experiment, in which he wrote: Practicality has been a feature of American life from the start, and a reason for the country's success. Americans on the whole eschewed ideology. We judged ideas by whether they worked. When they didn't, we tried something else. A strange contemporary exception to that tradition is the war on drugs.

By any rational test it is an overwhelming failure. Yet our leading politicians persist in calling for ever more stringent measures to enforce the policy of total prohibition, and do their best to prevent even a discussion of alternatives.

Dr. Lewis' MD group is likely to become a force in this issue. Politicians have adopted our current harsh policies with the nominal objective of solving the problem of drug abuse. Dr. Lewis personally, and the nationwide membership of his group, comprise the elite of the nation's addiction scientists (Dr. Lewis was so recognized last month by the Am. Medical Assoc.), and other medical specialists. The thesis of Physicians Leadership is that the drug war has no basis whatsoever in addiction science, that its conduct has worsened, rather than helped reduce, the nation's drug abuse problems. Elliot Richardson's attendance was canceled due to a family health emergency, but his statement of support for the forum, expressing his concern about the nation's current drug policies, will be delivered to begin the forum.

Ed Note: Michael Cutler (cutlermj@aol.com) is a member of the NORML Legal Committee and VCL Executive Director Richard Evans (emr@javanet.com) is a member of the NORML Board of Directors. Both are old friends. This forum is a manifestation of the establishment's recognition of the unacceptable cost of the "drug war" and represents a new willingness -- not only to "think the unthinkable" -- but to discuss it in public.
